newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy ex-Publitalia boss gets five-year sentence.
newsitem.headline: Italy ex-Publitalia boss gets five-year sentence.

text.p: A Italian court on Wednesday sentenced Marcello Dell'Utri, ex-chairman of Silvio Berlusconi's Publitalia advertising company, to three years in jail and fined him eight million lire ($5,300) for false billing and tax fraud.
Another ex-manager of the advertising company, Vincenzo Lupo Stanghellini, was sentenced to one year and three months in jail and finded four million lire.
Public prosecutors Luigi Marini and Cristina Bianconi had sought a five-year jail term for Dell'Ultri, and an 18-month term for Stanghellini.
According to the charges, Dell'Utri was aware of inflated bills for sporting sponsorships which were not recorded in the company's books.

Dell'Ultri had denied any wrongdoing. His lawyer, Oreste Dominioni, said the only person responsible for the affair was Gianpaolo Prandelli, former Publitalia deputy general manager, who accepted a reduced 18-month prison sentence under a plea-bargaining deal before the trial began.
Under Italian law, the sentence is not definitive until an appeal process has been completed. ($1=1516 Lire)
